description: The penalty encoding turns a constrained problem over binary variables into a QUBO model, an energy `offset + Σ aᵢ·xᵢ + Σ bᵢⱼ·xᵢ·xⱼ` with no side conditions. Each constraint adds a quadratic penalty with a weight `P` that the caller picks: `P·(1 − Σ xᵢ)²` for *exactly one*, `P·xᵢ·xⱼ` per pair for *at most one*, and `P·(Σ aᵢ·xᵢ + s − rhs)²` for a linear constraint, whose slack `s` gets new bits weighted 1, 2, 4, … and a remainder, so it reaches exactly its maximum. With integer coefficients a penalty is 0 when its constraint holds and at least `P` otherwise; the builder takes `P` as given, `penalty::safe` bounds it from the objective so every ground state is feasible, `penalty::tune` doubles it until a sampler returns feasible samples, and the decoder checks the constraints on the original variables. The model converts exactly to an Ising model over spins `s = 2x − 1` and back: integer models scale every energy by 4 so the halves and quarters stay whole, and float models keep a scale of 1. Use it to hand a planning problem, such as assigning tasks to agents with capacities, to a QUBO sampler or an annealer.

papers.title: Ising formulations of many NP problems
